mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer demand measured by HOUST coincides with stronger S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days due to increased investor confidence in corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns show no statistically significant correlation with HOUST in the same window (Pearson's r < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A surge in employment growth (PAYEMS) predicts higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days as labor market strength supports corporate optimism.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative despite PAYEMS growth exceeding the 90th percentile over the past 12 months.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) accelerates above its 12-month moving average, it anticipates supply-chain easing that boosts S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20-day windows following such acceleration events (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the CPIAUCSL inflation rate triggers a sharp S&P 500 decline in the following 20-day window as investors anticipate tighter policy.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2.0% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically different from the prior 20-day average during inflation spikes (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising unemployment rates (UNRATE) predict negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns as market anticipates economic slowdown.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day returns remain positive despite two consecutive months of UNRATE increases (p < 0.05 two-tailed test).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strength in both consumer (HOUST) and business demand (RSAFS) over the next 20 days creates a compounding positive effect on S&P 500 forward pricing.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive only when either HOUST or RSAFS alone is strong (multivariate Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains persistently below 1% for three consecutive months, it signals accommodative policy that drives S&P 500 60-day forward returns higher.
failure_condition: 60-day returns show no significant deviation from the 30-day average during such periods (Bayesian IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a rebound within 20 days predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as market anticipates supply-chain normalization.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < INDPRO_12mo_avg then INDPRO > INDPRO_12mo_avg in the next month
failure_condition: No significant return in 20 days after such a pattern (95% CI includes zero).
